title: Accounts Assistant
description:
If you're a Finance Administrator who enjoys getting stuck into the detail, taking ownership of your workload and being part of a business where your contribution actually matters, this could be worth a look.

This is a varied role, you'll be looking after the day-to-day transactional finance, keeping things running smoothly and supporting the Management Accountant with month-end reporting.

There's a good mix of responsibility here, and you'll have the opportunity to get involved in more than just processing invoices.

What you'll be doing:
- Managing the sales and purchase ledgers, including invoicing, allocations and supplier payments.
- Looking after credit control and keeping on top of outstanding balances.
- Completing bank and credit card reconciliations.
- Preparing payment runs and processing employee expenses.
- Assisting with VAT returns.
- Supporting the Management Accountant with month-end accounts, including accruals, prepayments and balance sheet reconciliations.
- Monitoring company expenditure and maintaining accurate financial records.
- Dealing with finance queries and supporting the wider business with general administration.

What do you need?

You'll ideally have experience in a similar role, with an understanding of transactional finance.

Experience using Sage and Excel would be useful, along with the ability to manage your own workload without needing someone to constantly look over your shoulder.

More importantly, you'll be organised, reliable and comfortable dealing with people across the business.

You don't need to be someone who wants to become a Finance Director in five years. If you're good at what you do, enjoy working in finance and want a role where you're trusted to get on with things, that's absolutely fine.

What's on offer?
- An annual salary of up to £30k (depending on experience)
- Hybrid working (2 days WFH)
- 28 days annual leave + birthday + stats
- Access to company benefits package after probation

Interested? Click "apply now" to find out more.

title: Finance Assistant
description:
Consortium Professional Recruitment are working with an established organisation in Pocklington to find a Finance Assistant who enjoys being involved, taking responsibility and making sure things happen when they should. You'll be joining a team where your contribution will be valued, with the opportunity to work across several areas of finance rather than being limited to one particular task.

The Opportunity:
As a Finance Assistant, you'll be involved in the financial activities that help keep a busy organisation running effectively.

You'll have the opportunity to:
- Process accurate monthly payroll, including PAYE, workplace pensions, P60s and P11 Ds.
- Maintain purchase and sales ledgers, process invoices, expenses and supplier payments, and assist with credit control.
- Complete bank and credit card reconciliations, administer petty cash and maintain fixed asset records.
- Support month-end and year-end activities, VAT returns and annual accounts preparation.
- Your work will directly contribute to a well-organised finance function, supporting informed decisions and helping the wider organisation operate with confidence.

About You:
You might already be working in an accounts team, supporting payroll or handling a mixture of finance responsibilities. What's important is that you're comfortable with numbers, enjoy finding solutions and can be relied upon to follow things through.

We're particularly interested in hearing from people who bring:
- Practical experience in finance or payroll, with an understanding of how accurate financial information supports a business.
- The confidence to work with spreadsheets, financial systems and detailed information.
- A methodical approach, with the ability to spot when something doesn't look quite right.
- The initiative to manage your own workload while knowing when to ask questions or involve others.
- A friendly, professional manner and the ability to build positive working relationships.
- Knowledge of Sage or Xero would be useful.

If you're studying towards AAT that's an added bonus.

The Benefits and Package:
In return, you'll enjoy:
- £29,000 to £32,000 depending on experience.
- Life insurance, healthcare scheme, company pension and 25 holidays + bank holidays
- A broad role offering exposure to payroll, financial accounting, reporting and audit processes.
- Opportunity to develop your career and complete further qualifications.
- Collaborative team working alongside an experienced and supportive Finance Manager

How to Apply:
If you're a Finance Assistant looking for a role with greater variety, or you're currently working in accounts or payroll and ready for your next move, we'd be pleased to hear from you!

This exciting Finance Assistant / Payroll Administrator opportunity is being managed by Consortium Professional Recruitment, a trusted recruitment partner with a Human First approach.

If you're ready to take the next step in your finance career, we'd love to hear from you. Please apply with your CV attached.

title: Employment & Litigation Legal Assistant
description:
Legal Assistant - Employment & Litigation

Location: York (with occasional travel between offices)
Salary: Competitive + Benefits
Job Type: Full-Time, Permanent

The Opportunity

An established and highly respected regional law firm is seeking a proactive and organised Legal Assistant to join its Employment & Litigation team.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone looking to develop their legal career within a supportive, professional environment. The successful candidate will play a key role in supporting fee earners, managing client onboarding, progressing legal matters, and ensuring excellent client service throughout the lifecycle of a case.

The role combines legal administration, compliance responsibilities and hands-on case support, making it ideal for an ambitious individual with previous legal experience or a strong interest in litigation and employment law.

Key Responsibilities
Client Onboarding & Matter Management
- Open and maintain client files using the firm's case management system.
- Create and manage matter records and ensure documentation is accurately recorded.
- Coordinate the issuance and return of client care documentation and engagement paperwork.
- Manage electronic signature processes and client onboarding administration.
- Act as a key point of contact for clients throughout the lifespan of a matter.

Compliance & Risk
- Conduct identity verification and Anti-Money Laundering (AML) checks.
- Maintain accurate compliance records and client documentation.
- Liaise with internal compliance teams regarding queries or potential concerns.
- Ensure client information is handled confidentially and in accordance with regulatory requirements.
- Support continuous improvement of processes and systems.

Litigation & Employment Support
- Assist fee earners in progressing a varied caseload.
- Draft legal correspondence and documentation under supervision.
- Organise and review client documents and case papers.
- Prepare bills, invoices and associated financial records.
- Undertake basic legal research and support case preparation activities.
- Ensure all work is completed in accordance with firm procedures and quality standards.

File Closure & Administration
- Coordinate file closure procedures and record maintenance.
- Ensure all compliance and financial matters are concluded appropriately.
- Support archiving and retrieval of both physical and electronic files.
- Assist with diary management, correspondence, filing and general administrative duties.
- Provide occasional reception cover when required.

About You

The successful candidate will possess:
- Previous experience within a law firm, legal support, compliance or professional services environment.
- Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage multiple priorities.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
- High levels of attention to detail and accuracy.
- Experience using Microsoft Office, particularly Word and Excel.
- Confidence working with digital document management and case management systems.
- A client-focused approach with a professional and empathetic manner.
- The ability to work both independently and collaboratively.
- A proactive attitude and willingness to learn and develop professionally.

Desirable Experience
- Experience supporting Employment, Litigation or Dispute Resolution teams.
- Knowledge of AML and client onboarding procedures.
- Familiarity with legal document drafting and case administration.
- Experience of electronic case management systems.

What's On Offer?
- The opportunity to join a well-established and reputable regional law firm.
- Exposure to a broad range of Employment and Litigation matters.
- Supportive team environment and ongoing professional development.
- Genuine opportunities for progression and career growth.
- Competitive salary and benefits package.

To apply, please submit your CV for confidential consideration.

Search is an equal opportunities recruiter and we welcome applications from all suitably skilled or qualified applicants, regardless of their race, sex, disability, religion/beliefs, sexual orientation or age.

title: HR Assistant (Maternity Cover)
description:
HR Assistant (Maternity Cover)
York/Hybrid
£24,839.36 per annum (FTE £31,049.20 per annum)
12 Months Fixed Term Contract, Part Time (28 hours per week)

We re looking for an organised and proactive HR Assistant to join our People Shared Services team on a 12-month maternity cover contract.

About the role

Working as part of a busy People Team, you ll provide a high-quality HR administration service across the employee lifecycle, supporting areas including recruitment, employee changes, absence, learning and development and employee benefits.

You ll maintain accurate and confidential employee records, process new starters and changes on our HR and payroll system, prepare contracts and other HR documentation and respond to queries from colleagues, candidates and managers. You ll also support pre-employment and compliance checks, including right to work, references and DBS checks, as well as Occupational Health referrals and regular data audits.

As a first point of contact for general HR enquiries, you ll provide straightforward guidance on policies and processes, escalating more complex matters where appropriate. You ll also have the opportunity to support wider People Team projects and identify ways we can continue to improve our systems and processes.

This is a varied role where accuracy, organisation and great customer service are key.

About you

You ll have solid experience of HR administration within a busy environment and a good understanding of employment legislation and HR processes. Highly organised and able to manage competing priorities, you ll have excellent attention to detail and be confident working accurately to deadlines. You ll be a strong communicator who can build positive relationships with colleagues at all levels and provide a friendly, professional and responsive service.

You ll be comfortable using Microsoft Office applications including Word, Excel and Outlook, as well as HR software systems, and will be confident handling sensitive and confidential information. You ll be proactive, flexible and willing to use your initiative to solve problems and improve ways of working.

A CIPD/Level 3 qualification would be advantageous but are not essential.

How to apply

If you share our passion and this role sounds like you, then we re looking forward to hearing from you.

Please submit your CV and supporting information via our online application platform.

The closing date for applications is 8th November 2026

Interviews will take place on tbc

We reserve the right to bring the closing date forward should enough quality applications be received prior to the current closing date.

Additional Information

Applications are welcome from all, regardless of age, disability, marriage or civil partnership, pregnancy or maternity, religion or belief, race, sex, sexual orientation, trans status or socioeconomic background.

We positively encourage applications from people from marginalised backgrounds, including but not limited to those with experience of living in poverty.

We are committed to being an anti-racist organisation and operate an anonymised recruitment process so that bias is eliminated from the shortlisting process.

In support of our approach to flexible working, we are happy to receive applications from those seeking full-time employment, as well as those who may want to share the role on a part-time basis. When making your application, please state whether you want to be considered for either full or part-time work and, if part-time, the number of hours per week you would be looking for.

At JRF we re at our best when we re continually building on trust, showing we care and making a difference and hope others will do the same. So, for those roles which allow it, we re developing a more blended approach to how and where you work. This means you can expect to work flexibly between the office and home with an expectation of one day in the office a week.

We offer a supportive and flexible workplace. For details about our benefits click here: JRF Benefits

We are a Disability Confident Employer. This means that we are committed to the recruitment, progression and retention of disabled individuals. We shall also offer interviews to disabled candidates who meet the minimum criteria for the job. If you have a disability, please tell us if you would like to be considered for an interview under the Disability Confident Scheme.

If you have any additional needs and need reasonable adjustments to be made to the interview process, please let us know.

title: Practice Administrator
description:
Practice Administrator Location: Richmond, Surrey
Salary: £30,000 per annum, plus a twice-yearly bonus
Hours: Full-time, with flexible working
Holiday: 25 days plus bank holidays
About the role We are an established practice in Richmond, looking for a highly organised administrator to take ownership of our clients Companies House and statutory administration.
This is a company secretary-style role at the heart of the practice. You will make sure our clients filings are accurate and on time, that the right people receive the right requests, and that nothing slips through the gaps. It suits someone who takes pride in process, accuracy and follow-through.
Key responsibilities
- Manage Companies House administration across our client portfolio, including confirmation statements, director and shareholder updates, registered office changes and annual filing deadlines
- Maintain statutory registers and company records accurately and up to date
- Issue requests for information and documents to the right people within client organisations, and follow up until they are resolved
- Keep a clear diary of filing deadlines and flag risks to the accountants early
- Handle client data and correspondence in line with GDPR, including secure storage, sharing and record retention
- Open, log and distribute incoming post
- Answer the telephone and greet callers professionally, directing queries to the right team member
- Provide general administrative support to the practice, including filing, document preparation and diary coordination

About you Essential
- Experience in an administrative, company secretarial, legal or professional services setting
- Excellent organisation and attention to detail, with a methodical approach to deadlines
- Confident, clear written and spoken communication, including a professional telephone manner
- A sound working understanding of GDPR and confidentiality
- Good IT skills, including Microsoft Office

Desirable
- Experience of Companies House filing or company secretarial work
- Experience working in an accountancy practice or law firm
- Familiarity with practice management or company secretarial software

We welcome applications from people with transferable experience, for example from legal, conveyancing, compliance or other regulated administration roles.
What we offer
- Salary of £30,000
- Bonus paid twice a year
- 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays
- Flexible working arrangements e.g. flexible start and finish times

Project Administrator

Salary: £25,500 to £30,000 per annum, depending on skills and experience
Location: Selby, North Yorkshire (office-based, average 4 days per week with occasional home working)
Hours: Monday to Friday, 8.30am to 5.00pm
Contract: Full-time, permanent
Benefits: 25 days' holiday plus bank holidays, discretionary bonus, pension, training and development, free parking and hybrid working

What We Offer
- Salary of £25,500 to £30,000, depending on experience.
- 25 days' annual leave plus bank holidays.
- Discretionary performance-related bonus scheme.
- Company pension scheme.
- Cycle to work scheme.
- Free on-site parking.
- Regular company and team events.
- Occasional home working, with an average of four days per week in the office.
- Funded training and professional development opportunities.
- A supportive working environment within a growing business.

About Innovex Group

Innovex Group is a growing commercial fit-out and refurbishment contractor based in Selby, North Yorkshire, delivering projects across the UK.

We work with clients across education, healthcare, care and the public sector, providing high-quality construction and refurbishment solutions where safety, compliance and attention to detail are essential.

We are a close-knit, ambitious team where everyone plays an important part in the success of the business.

Due to continued growth, we are looking for an organised and proactive Project Administrator to join our team.

The Role

This is a varied and busy position, providing essential administrative support to our Estimating and Project Delivery teams.

You will help keep projects running smoothly by coordinating documentation, ordering materials, supporting site teams and ensuring information is accurate and up to date.

Working closely with project managers, suppliers and subcontractors, you will be involved in different stages of the project lifecycle, making this an excellent opportunity to develop your career within the construction industry.

Key Responsibilities
- Provide day-to-day administrative support to the Estimating and Project Delivery teams.
- Assist with purchasing materials, raising orders and tracking deliveries to site.
- Support project managers and site teams with enquiries, online orders, signage and general administration.
- Prepare site files, project documentation and mobilisation paperwork.
- Maintain accurate project records in line with company procedures and ISO management systems.
- Assist with subcontractor pre-qualification questionnaires and maintain supplier and subcontractor records.
- Coordinate company vehicle administration, including servicing, MOTs, insurance and mileage records.
- Answer incoming calls and direct enquiries to the appropriate team members.
- Provide general administrative support across the business, ensuring tasks are completed accurately and on time.

Location: Scarborough

Salary: Competitive.

Job type: Full Time - Permanent. Mon-Thurs 8.30am-16.50pm & Friday 8.30am-15.10pm. Potentially after training some hybrid working.

We want all our colleagues to grow and build careers with Dale. We invest in our people for the future.

Many of our team members have been with us for over 30 years and some of our management team began their careers as apprentices. As we have grown so too have they and that knowledge is passed down as our team develops and evolves.

No two days are the same and variety is a key part of life for our team at Dale. There's always an opportunity to learn new skills and progress your career. We want to be a great place to work that is diverse and inclusive which is why we focus on supporting people and their development.

The role:

Identify planned, remedial and reactive works, efficiently coordinate available engineers, specialist tools and materials to the site following customers access requirements. Control invoicing, forecasts and work closely with the contract manager to deliver contractual requirements and any customer escalations.

Why you're our kind of person:

We're not looking for people who sit down and say, 'that'll do', we're driven by doing the right thing for our customers. We operate in an agile fast paced environment, and we are always looking forward, improving, never settling and wanting to be the difference for our customers. It's an exciting time to join the energy industry as we seek to reduce our reliance on fossil fuels and our ambitions present a tremendous opportunity. We work hard to deliver, and there's a lot to do, but the ability to make an impact in our business is significant. So, if that resonates with you and you want to love our customers as we do then come join a team of like-minded people

What good looks like:
- Seamless: You'll provide high quality solutions to our customers
- Specialist: You'll be skilled in your area, be an expert in a number of Dale processes and be commercially smart.
- Collaborative: You'll advise your colleagues and input into other work, and also be able to work independently to get the job done.

What you'll do:
- Provide primary point of contact to customers.
- Forecasting and contract scheduling of all planned and reactive service-related issues.
- Control of documentation to support the delivery of the contract visits such as Engineer permits, authorisations, inductions, and RAMS etc.
- Review and closure of all customer queries, including billing and Purchase Order amendments or uplifts.
- Ensure that key personnel are kept informed of customer requirements and any significant issues.
- Raise and co-ordinate warranty claims and contract repairs in line with customer expectations.
- Work efficiently and effectively with the Project Managers and other areas or departments to fulfil overall company objectives.
- Liaise with other coordinators and Service Support to maximise efficiencies and ensure customers' requirements are met.
- To contribute to the achievement of department and business KPI objectives.
- Complete any reasonable task as directed by the Contracts Manager.

What's important to us:

Experience:
- 2+ years working in a similar role in the service industry.
- Good negotiation and influencing skills.
- Excellent planning and organisational skills.
- Experienced at working with MS Outlook/Word/Excel and PDF documents, though training will be provided.
- Excellent communication and customer service skills.
- Team player as well as ability to work on own initiative.
- You'll be passionate about health and safety and ensuring that everyone goes home from work safely from our projects.
- You'll communicate openly, transparently, and effectively to ensure a high level of customer service.
- You'll be resilient and thrive in a fast-paced environment.
- You'll be inquisitive and stay up to date with industry and technical changes and legislation.
- You'll be keen to work collaboratively with others to develop shared solutions.
- You'll have good levels of self-awareness, excellent interpersonal and communication skills.
- You'll have good time management skills.

Our values:

Do the right thing.

Be the difference.

Love our customers.

Never settle.

Look forward.

Please click on the APPLY button to send your CV for this role.

Candidates with the relevant experience or job titles of: Service Coordinator, Service Delivery Coordinator, Contract Coordinator, Contracts Coordinator, Operations Coordinator, Field Service Coordinator, Maintenance Coordinator, Planned Works Coordinator, Reactive Works Coordinator, Engineering Coordinator, Engineer Scheduler, Service Scheduler, Scheduling Coordinator, Customer Service Coordinator, Contract Support Coordinator, Service Operations Coordinator, will also be considered for this role.

title: Care & Support Coordinator
description:
Care & Support Coordinator

Location: Harrogate

Salary: £16.10 per hour

Are you organised, proactive and passionate about delivering high-quality, person-centred care? We would love to hear from you!

We are recruiting for a Care & Support Coordinator to provide cover across weekdays, evenings and weekends. We welcome applications from candidates seeking either full-time or part-time employment.

Whether you are looking for full-time hours, part-time work, we would be pleased to hear from you.

About the Role

We are looking for a dedicated and experienced Care & Support Coordinator to join our team and play a key role in the effective planning and delivery of our care and support services.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone with experience in social care who enjoys coordinating people, supporting staff and ensuring customers receive high-quality, consistent and personalised care.

Working closely with the Manager, Deputy Manager, staff, customers, families and other professionals, you will support the smooth day-to-day running of the service, ensuring that care and support are effectively coordinated and individual needs are met.

You will play an important role in ensuring the right staff are in the right place at the right time, while promoting a person-centred approach that places customers' rights, choices, wishes and independence at the heart of everything we do.

Key Responsibilities

Care Planning and Coordination
- Plan, book and coordinate care and support visits.
- Coordinate and manage staff rotas, ensuring appropriate staffing levels and cover across the service.
- Allocate staff to customers, taking account of individual needs, staff skills, experience, location and compatibility.
- Ensure all rota changes are updated promptly and accurately on the rostering system.
- Assess and process referrals and coordinate the onboarding of new customers.
- Develop, review and maintain customer support plans and risk assessments.
- Maintain effective communication with customers, families, staff and other professionals involved in the delivery of care and support.

Service Quality and Staff Support
- Support the Manager with the effective day-to-day running of the care and support service.
- Promote and monitor the delivery of high-quality, personalised care and support.
- Undertake spot checks and staff supervisions as required.
- Support recruitment and selection activities.
- Manage staff absence procedures, including conducting return-to-work interviews.
- Promote a positive, supportive and professional working environment.

Operational Responsibilities
- Respond to emergency call bells and provide background support when working at St Roberts Grove.
- Provide cover for care and support calls when required.
- Participate in an out-of-hours on-call rota.
- Attend staff meetings, supervision sessions and training as required.
- Promote a positive image of the organisation, its work and values.
- Maintain compliance with organisational policies and procedures, including relevant health and safety requirements.

What We Are Looking For

We are seeking someone who is proactive, reliable and well organised, with the ability to manage competing priorities, use their initiative and work effectively as part of a team.

You will have good communication and administrative skills, an understanding of the social care sector and the confidence to coordinate staff and respond effectively to the changing needs of the service.

Essential Requirements

Skills and Competencies
- Good verbal and written communication skills.
- Ability to plan, organise and coordinate staff rotas effectively.
- Strong administrative skills and good computer literacy.
- Ability to maintain accurate records and follow statutory reporting procedures.
- Ability to understand, implement and follow policies, procedures and instructions.

Experience
- Experience of working within the social care sector.
- Previous experience of coordinating staff rotas.

Qualifications and Knowledge
- Minimum Level 2 qualification in Health and Social Care, with a willingness to work towards Level 3.
- Knowledge of health and safety within care services, including risk assessment and management.
- Understanding of safeguarding, including the ability to recognise signs of abuse and follow the appropriate reporting procedures.

Additional Requirements
- Willingness to work flexibly to meet the changing needs of the service.
- Commitment to keeping knowledge, skills and professional practice up to date.
- Willingness to undertake an Enhanced DBS check.

Desirable Requirements
- Experience of staff management or supervision.
- Experience of using care management or rostering systems.
- Full, valid UK driving licence.

What We Offer

This is an opportunity to make a real difference to the lives of the people we support while developing your skills and experience within a rewarding social care environment.

You will be joining a team that is committed to promoting independence, dignity, choice and high-quality, person-centred care.

Equality, Diversity and Inclusion

We are committed to promoting equality, diversity and inclusion and welcome applications from all sections of the community.

To Apply

If you feel you are a suitable candidate and would like to work for Disability Action Yorkshire, please do not hesitate to apply.

We handle all our recruitment in-house and agencies don't need to reach out. Duties may vary from time to time but these will include: Providing a reception service for the centre Interacting and communicating with patients, clinicians and other staff this may involve re-booking appointments, providing advice and assistance Computer data entry/data allocation and collation; processing and recording information Filing and retrieving paperwork both manually and electronically Participate in meetings as required Escalation of issues to the Estates and facilities Manager if required e.g. facilities, Health & Safety Provide administrative cover in the event of holiday and sickness Manage and prioritise own workload Recognise and work within own competence To provide and receive routine information verbally or electronically to inform work colleagues and key stakeholders To demonstrate a competent level of interpersonal skills when providing information Provide payroll support with invoice processing Provide administrative support with monthly reporting submissions Support with rota fill / clinical staffing where appropriate Main Duties and Responsibilities: Duties may vary from time to time - but these will include: Business responsibilities: Maintain ethos and culture of Nimbuscare Limited. Positively promote Nimbuscare Limited both in and out of the workplace Attend educational and staff meetings as requested. To support the introduction of new working processes to optimise quality. To build and maintain relationships with relevant personnel Learning and development: You will participate in any training programme implemented by Nimbuscare Limited as part of this employment, such training to include: Participation in individual performance reviews, including maintaining a record of own personal and/or professional development. Make effective use of learning opportunities within and outside the workplace Undertake mandatory and statutory training as required. Team working: Work as an effective and responsible team member, supporting others and exploring the mechanisms to develop new ways of working. Accept delegation from senior staff, prioritise own workload and ensure effective time management strategies are embedded in own practice. Participate in team activities that create opportunities to improve patient care. Contribute to the effectiveness of the team by reflecting on own and team activities and making suggestions on ways to improve and enhance the teams performance. Confidentiality: To understand and be aware of the confidentiality of information gained during the course of your duties, which may include access to personal information relating to clients, patients and members of staff. It is expected that you understand the importance of treating information in a discreet and confidential manner. Health & Safety: Identifying the risks involved in work activities and undertaking such activities in a way that manages those risks. Making effective use of training to update knowledge and skills. Using appropriate infection control procedures, maintaining work areas in a tidy and safe way and free from hazards. Reporting potential risks within Acomb Garth identified. Equality and Diversity: To actively support equality, diversity and inclusion and ensure that all work colleagues, patients and staff are valued and treated with dignity and respect. Quality: Alert other team members to issues of quality and risk. Assess own performance and take accountability for own actions, either directly or under supervision. Effectively manage own time, workload and resources. Work within own limitations and experience. Be aware of and co-operate with audit. Work effectively with individuals in other agencies to meet patients needs. Portray a professional image at all times. Communication: Communicate effectively with colleagues, patients and external parties Recognise and have awareness of peoples needs for alternative methods of communication and respond accordingly. Other: This job description is neither exhaustive nor exclusive and will be reviewed periodically in conjunction with you.

advertiser_name: Tees Esk and Wear Valleys NHS Foundation Trust
description: This vacancy is part time for 22.5hrs per week working Monday, Wednesday and Thursday 9am to 5pm. We are looking for an experienced, self-motivated individual to provide administration and secretarial support to our Scarborough, Whitby and Ryedale Community Learning Disability Team. The team forms part of a wider North Yorkshire LD Service across our 4 Community Teams based in York, Harrogate, Northallerton and Scarborough providing support to service users, carers and their families locally. As the Community Team Administrator, you will be a key member of the team providing administration and secretarial support to the local Multi-Disciplinary Team (MDT) supporting daily huddles, referrals, arranging meetings and appointments along with processing letters and reports, ensuring they are recorded on the trusts electronic patients' records. You must have the Right to Work in the UK in order to be successfully appointed to this role. Please note, this role does not meet the required eligibility criteria for sponsorship under the Skilled Worker visa and therefore the Trust is unable to offer sponsorship for this particular role. You will be part of a small administration team working together to support a Receptionists and Medical Secretaries to provide a professional and efficient service to our service users, carers and other colleagues from our community teams. You will support the daily clinical huddles, processing any referrals or administration work that is required and back up front of house enquiries during breaks and absences. Dealing with referrals to the team and taking appropriate action to process and accurately record relevant information on the trusts patient records or data bases following standard work. Provide a comprehensive secretarial service by processing and storing appropriate correspondence and undertake any general office duties as required e.g. printing, copying etc. Manage diaries as required for members of the clinical team. Arrange meetings, including booking venues, organising catering, provide administration support to appropriate meetings ensuring that papers are distributed and any other administration follow up actions as required. First point of contact for service users, family and carers, responding to a range of enquiries or concerns over the telephone. This may involve arranging for an interpreter. Service users have a range of mental health conditions and or learning disabilities. Processes referrals, letters, emails, reports for clinical staff and Team Manager ensuring appropriate action is taken on the trust patient system. Manages diaries and appointments for clinical staff. Provides comprehensive secretarial service to clinical staff and Team Manager within the team including any appropriate general office duties as required Please refer to the attached job description and person specification for further detailed information to ensure that you meet the role criteria before applying. Please contact the team on 01723 580940 if you would like to arrange an informal visit.

title: Medical Receptionist
description: We're looking for committed, enthusiastic people to join our innovative multi-disciplinary team based in York's newest purpose-built primary care facility. As the successful candidate, you will be a key part of our two partner practice and will work alongside a growing team. You will be the first point of contact for patients and be responsible for receiving, assisting, and signposting patients in accessing the appropriate service in a courteous, efficient, and effective way. You will also provide general assistance to the practice team. At Unity Health, the main way that patients contact us is via email or phone depending on the patient's preference. We do not make patients complete an online form so all contact made by a patient to the surgery will be answered by a member of Unity Health staff. Unity Health currently operates 2 surgeries to the South and East of York, close to excellent local amenities. We are a consistently high QoF achiever, a supporting member of the Humber & North Yorkshire ICB and an active member of the Student Health Association (SHA). The main duties as a medical receptionist at Unity Health will include: - Being the first point of contact for all people contacting the surgery in person, via email and on the telephone. This can be people from patients and their carers to delivery men and contractors. - Accurately signposting patients to the most appropriate service/person for their need using training provided and resources made available. - Providing assistance to the wider team in the surgery. - Projecting a positive and friendly image of the surgery. - Booking and amending appointments appropriately. - Play a huge role in the day to day running of the surgery to ensure that things run smoothly. - Report any concerns to the relevant persons at the earliest opportunity. - Have strong IT skills which are vital to this role JOB TITLE: Medical Receptionist REPORTS TO: Managine partner, Executive Assistant and Operations Lead HOURS: Various TBA, Monday to Friday Overview First point of contact for patients, both on the reception desks and phones. Receive, assist and signpost patients in accessing the appropriate service or healthcare professional in a courteous, efficient and effective way. Provide general assistance to the Practice team and project a positive and friendly image to patients and other visitors, either in person or via the telephone. Provide efficient, helpful, informative and supportive reception and administration services to patients and members of the Practice team. The candidate must have experience working with the general public, not necessarily in a healthcare setting. IT skills are vital to this role. Responsibilities 1. Health & Safety The post-holder will assist in promoting and maintaining their own and others health, safety and security as defined in the Practice Health & Safety Policy, to include: Using personal security systems within the workplace according to Practice guidelines Identifying the risks involved in work activities and undertaking such activities in a way that manages those risks Making effective use of training to update knowledge and skills Using appropriate infection control procedures, maintaining work areas in a tidy and safe way and free from hazards Reporting potential risks identified 2. Quality The post holder will strive to maintain quality within the Practice, and will: To work within the clinical computer system to improve and maintain data quality Alert other team members to issues of quality and risk Assess own performance and take accountability for own actions, either directly or under supervision Contribute to the effectiveness of the team by reflecting on own and team activities and making suggestions on ways to improve and enhance the teams performance Work effectively with individuals in other agencies to meet patients needs Effectively manage own time, workload and resources 3. Confidentiality In the course of seeking treatment, patients entrust us with, or allow us to gather, sensitive information in relation to their health and other matters. They do so in confidence and have the right to expect that staff will respect their privacy and act appropriately In the performance of the duties outlined in this Job Description, the post-holder may have access to confidential information relating to patients and their carers, Practice staff and other healthcare workers. They may also have access to information relating to the Practice as a business organisation. All such information from any source is to be regarded as strictly confidential Information relating to patients, carers, colleagues, other healthcare workers or the business of the Practice may only be divulged to authorised persons in accordance with the Practice policies and procedures relating to confidentiality and the protection of personal and sensitive data 4. Equality and Diversity The post-holder will support the equality, diversity and rights of patients, carers and colleagues, to include: Acting in a way that recognizes the importance of peoples rights, interpreting them in a way that is consistent with Practice procedures and policies, and current legislation Respecting the privacy, dignity, needs and beliefs of patients, carers and colleagues Behaving in a manner which is welcoming to and of the individual, is non-judgmental and respects their circumstances, feelings priorities and rights. 5. Personal/Professional Development The post-holder will participate in any training programme implemented by the Practice as part of this employment, such training to include: Participation in an annual individual performance review, including taking responsibility for maintaining a record of own personal and/or professional development Taking responsibility for own development, learning and performance and demonstrating skills and activities to others who are undertaking similar work 6. Communication The post holder should recognise the importance of effective communication within the team and will strive to: Communicate effectively with other team members, patients and carers Recognise peoples needs for alternative methods of communication and respond accordingly 7. Contribution to the Implementation of Services The post holder will: Apply Practice policies, standards and guidance Discuss with other members of the team how the policies, standards and guidelines will affect own work Participate in audit where appropriate Safeguarding Children Under section 11 of the Children Act 2004 all NHS staff must ensure that their functions are discharged with regard to the need to safeguard and promote the welfare of children (Working Together to Safeguard Children, HM Government, 2018). All staff need to ensure, as part of their work with children and families and with adults who are parents or carers who are experiencing personal problems, that the needs of the children are considered and that where necessary they are assessed and appropriate referrals are made. Staff need to be aware of the relevant parts of What To Do If Youre Worried A Child Is Being Abused (2015) https://www.gov.uk/government/uploads/system/uploads/attachment_data/file/419604/What_to_do_if_you_re_worried_a_child_is_being_abused.pdf It is incumbent on all staff to ensure that they undertake child protection / safeguarding children training as per Safeguarding Children and Young people: roles and competences for health care staff Intercollegiate document (RCN, 2019). Safeguarding Adults Under sections 42 to 47 of the Care Act (2014) chapter 14 of the statutory guidance states: Safeguarding means protecting an adults right to live in safety, free from abuse and neglect. It is about people and organisations working together to prevent and stop both the risks and experience of abuse or neglect, while at the same time making sure that the adults wellbeing is promoted including, where appropriate, having regard to their views, wishes, feelings and beliefs in deciding on any action. Professionals should work with the adult to establish what being safe means to them and how that can be best achieved. All staff must comply with mandatory training requirements as per 'Adult Safeguarding: Roles and Competencies for Health Care Staff' (RCN, 2018) and ensure that adult safeguarding is embedded as an essential part of their daily practice. Safeguarding is everyones business and staff within the organisation have a particular responsibility to ensure all safeguarding concerns are responded to effectively and efficiently in accordance with the local Practice Safeguarding Adults Policy. http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2014/23/contents/enacted Notes This is not intended to be an exhaustive list of responsibilities, and it is expected that you will participate in a wide range of activities.

description: An opportunity has arisen for a confident and supportive administrator to join our busy and dedicated Crisis Resolution and Home Treatment team (CRHT) based at The Orchards in Ripon. This post is part-time, 34hours per week, Monday to Friday. The CRHT team operates 24-hours a day, providing advice and support to those seeking help in a mental health emergency or being referred by a healthcare professional for assessment and triage. Further information about our services can be found here CRHT services provided by TEWV The Orchards is a base of operations for multiple mental health teams working across North Yorkshire, County Durham and Teesside. The CRHT team are based here, as are the Early Intervention Psychosis team and there is an inpatient mental health recovery unit on site too. The site benefits from free parking and is easily accessible by car and bicycle. As a member of the CRHT team, you will work in an open plan office alongside clinicians and support staff. The office is an area of high activity, and no two days are the same. If you are looking for a new challenge, enjoy variety in your work and are looking to be part of a team striving to make a difference, we will welcome your application for this role. Please do consider making contact with the recruiting manager for an informal conversation prior to submitting an application, we'd like to hear from you . Whilst having extensive experience in an administrative role is essential, NHS or other health care experience is not. We are first and foremost looking for an individual with a passion for people, customer service experience, extensive organisational and digital data management skills, an interest in working in a health care setting and a 'can do' attitude. This role is at the heart of a cohesive and dedicated team and is a pivotal role in the day-to-day operations. You will work collaboratively with other administrators, closely with the clinicians and the team manager, to support them in ensuring high standards are maintained and that they have everything they need to provide the best possible care for service users. The successful candidate will be able to evidence that they are comfortable multi-tasking, are confident offering supervisory support to other administrative staff, can communicate confidently, build strong working relationships with a variety of people and can prioritise their workload. Duties will include comprehensive, pro-active and re-active diary management for the Consultants and medical team; processing of digital dictation and production of patient letters; minute taking; accurate and timely record keeping (confidential, sensitive and legal information) on the electronic patient record system. For full details please refer to the Job Description. For guidance on the application process, please refer to the TRAC helpful hints attached. With a starting salary of £28,392 per annum (pro-rata), a generous NHS pension scheme, a fantastic annual leave package (27 days annual leave plus bank holidays) and access to other NHS staff benefits and discounts, it is fair to say that this job has a lot to offer. And, its not just the NHS pay scale and benefits that we offer that make joining our organisation an excellent choice, there are many training and development opportunities available, giving you the opportunity for career progression. All staff have regular 1-2-1s, quarterly supervision meetings and an annual appraisal, which provides lots of opportunity for discussion around achievements, challenges and aspirations. Staff recognition is very important to us; we work closely with colleagues to support development, the staff voice, and to recognise teams and individuals through our Greatix and Star Award schemes; highlighting the outstanding work being done every day. We recognise that Administrators are professionals and are a valuable asset to our organisation. We understand that they have a key role in the support and delivery of our services and that their contribution helps us in achieving our aim of consistently providing safe and high quality care for our service users. The kind of care we would want for ourselves and for our loved ones. Please refer to the attached job description and person specification for further detailed information to ensure that you meet the role criteria before applying. You must have the Right to Work in the UK in order to be successfully appointed to this role. Please note, this role does not meet the required eligibility criteria for sponsorship under the Skilled Worker visa and therefore the Trust is unable to offer sponsorship for this particular role. This job advert may close early if a high volume of applications have been received. If interested, please apply for this post as soon as possible.
